A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same RepoReason benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support matching retained content against the expanded revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations across seven Python repositories, including accuracy tables, metric correlations, and reasoning-scope analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original evaluations and adds mutation/filtering ablations, partial correlations, temperature sensitivity results, failure cases, and trace-depth comparisons.

M1.justification: The masked-assertion task, execution-driven mutation, deterministic-value filtering, dynamic slicing, and ReadOnlyAgent procedure remain. Appendices D-F substantially expand implementation documentation without establishing a redesign of the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Python assertion reasoning using cachetools, toolz, yarl, networkx, jinja2, attrs, and sympy. The added controls and cases use this retained coverage; no additional language, repository domain, or task is introduced.

E2.justification: The five models in Tables 2-4 are retained. Figure 3 also retains its six-model comparison, including DeepSeek-v3.2 and Gemini-2.5-Flash. Changed plotted scores do not change comparator membership; the new ablations introduce component controls.

E3.justification: The main Pass@1 evaluation retains 2,492 tasks, temperature 0, and an 8,192-token limit. Added experiments introduce original-versus-mutated and unfiltered-versus-filtered controls, temperature 1.0, and bounded-versus-unbounded tracing on 651 samples. Figure 4 revises reported MCL/DFI sample counts from 2,490/2,221 to 2,492 each without explaining the revision.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial checks absent from v1: EDME and structural-filtering ablations in Section 4.4, partial correlations controlling the other metrics in Appendix B.3, temperature sensitivity in B.4, two integration-failure cases in G, and trace-depth sensitivity in H. These examine benchmark construction, confounding, robustness, and failure mechanisms.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 introduces partial-correlation estimates and p-values, whereas v1 reports ordinary Pearson coefficients without corresponding significance tests. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals for the main accuracy results. Changed distribution means and standard deviations are result changes.

E6.justification: Tables 2-4 retain their values, but Figures 2-4 change numerical results. For example, Figure 3 assigns Gemini-2.5-Flash cross-file accuracy 34.2% in v1 and 53.4% in v3. New results include DeepSeek's 73.15% without EDME versus 60.96% with EDME, Claude's 67.98% at temperature 1.0, partial correlations, and 6.2-fold trace inflation.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 newly defines pairwise memorization rate as Pr(pass_orig and not pass_mut), a limited formal addition. The existing complexity-scoring and symbolic-equivalence equations remain. Appendix F mainly makes existing metric computations explicit; it adds no theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: abductive assertion verification, execution-driven contamination mitigation, three diagnostic metrics, and integration width as the primary bottleneck. The added conclusion restates these claims; new supporting analyses do not redefine their scope.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes conceptual metric orthogonality from numerical correlation and interprets partial correlations as evidence for an independent DFI bottleneck. It adds constraint-integration explanations for failures, attributes temperature-stable patterns to architectural limitations, and defends the trace-depth cap as noise reduction. The limitations discussion also expands treatment of LLM participation and test generation.

D1.justification: Appendices C-I add worked prompts, input/output contracts, validation rules, pseudocode, slicing details, and the difficulty-labeling protocol. Table 9 newly specifies GPT-5.2 as mutation teacher, temperature 0.7, 16,384 tokens, three retries, and 180-second trials. These are disclosures rather than demonstrated setting changes. v1's explicit future open-source commitment is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds Shi et al.'s Codehacker as a prospective source of adversarial test-generation techniques. The benchmark comparisons and broader research positioning remain. Bibliographic corrections, such as the Jia and Harman publication year, concern existing references.

P1.justification: The existing construction and metric descriptions receive extensive step-by-step explanations, dedicated technical appendices, prompt documentation, and worked examples. v3 also adds a conclusion and acknowledgments and expands the limitations section. Much of the original main narrative remains, with smaller terminology and language edits.

P2.justification: Figures 2-4 are redrawn with revised legends, axes, styling, and metric titles; existing tables gain ranking emphasis and shading. v3 adds Tables 6-11, two algorithm displays, a three-stage mutation example in Figure 5, and additional prompt/code boxes. Numerical changes within these displays are separately assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: Detailed implementation documentation and new controls improve inspectability, but v3 introduces unresolved inconsistencies in central evidence. Figure 4 reports means 388.4/88.0/7.1 while Appendix B.2 retains 393.6/93.9/8.3; Table 8's temperature-0 correlations also disagree with Table 4. Figures 2-3 change reported accuracies without explaining the revisions. The PDFs do not resolve whether the evidential gains outweigh this loss of numerical consistency, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
